title: Euler's theorem: existence of Eulerian trails (Hierholzer, formalize-only)
why_not_classical: Euler 1736 / Hierholzer 1873: a finite connected graph has an Eulerian circuit iff every degree is even, and an Eulerian trail iff exactly 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree. Completely settled. Value is a Mathlib contribution (Trails.lean has IsEulerian + the necessary parity; the existence TODO is still open). Archive Konigsberg is a negative instance on a custom graph, not this theorem. Do NOT re-fund as novel.

statement_pin_required.convention: Fix G : SimpleGraph V, Fintype V, G.Connected. Let oddDeg = {v | Odd (G.degree v)}. If card oddDeg = 0 then ∃ circuit p, p.IsEulerian (with IsCircuit caveat: K_1 nil walk is Eulerian but not a circuit). If card oddDeg = 2 then ∃ Eulerian trail between those two vertices. Use Mathlib Walk.IsEulerian / IsCircuit.
landmines: Connectedness is essential (two disjoint even-degree components are a counterexample to '0-or-2 odd degrees ⇒ Eulerian'). Do not copy the Trails.lean TODO without G.Connected.
SimpleGraph has no parallel edges; do not formalize Königsberg (Archive already did a custom-graph negative instance).
Eulerian ≠ Hamiltonian. Do not re-prime Dirac.
0 odd ⇒ circuit; 2 odd ⇒ open trail. Finite only.
IsCircuit excludes the K_1 nil walk (STATEMENT caveat already in ProofLab/Eulerian.lean header).
Do NOT re-prime Level A K_1 / C_n / K_2.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: L. Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis, Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 8 (1736) 128–140. Constructive pin: C. Hierholzer, Math. Ann. 6 (1873) 30–32. Type pin: Mathlib SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian + SimpleGraph.Connected.
